newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Kanto Biomedical says seeks TSE listing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Kanto Biomedical says seeks TSE listing.

text.p: Clinical testing company Kanto Biomedical Laboratory Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it seeks to list its shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) by the year 2000.
Company president Yutaka Kannari told Reuters in an interview that his company was also considering raising its dividend for the year to May 1997.

"We would like to increase our sales in welfare projects for the aged to about a half of our overall sales by the year 2000. We also would like to list on the Tokyo bourse as a private welfare company," he said.

The company, which is based near Tokyo, was set up in 1976 and registered its shares on the over-the-counter market in 1990. It has 1,800 hospitals as customers and also sells computers and other electronic equipments.
The president said the firm's earnings for the current financial year to May 1997 would largely be the same with its earlier estimate announced in January.
At that time, the firm saw a nine percent rise in its sales to 10.6 billion yen and a 11 percent rise in its current profit to 1.6 billion yen.

He said the firm was mulling steps to pass on the benefits to its shareholders such as higher dividend in order to keep a pledge to keep its payout ratio -- the percentage of profits paid to shareholders in the form of dividends -- at 30 percent.
